summary: The Missouri Public Service Commission comments in support of the SPP Joint Movants' 95-day abeyance request in EL26-68, arguing good cause exists because SPP's Board meets November 17, one day outside the 90-day window.
ask: Grant the Joint Movants' request for a 95-day abeyance of the section 206 proceeding.

points.point: Missouri PSC says the 95 days fits SPP's November 17 Board meeting and state input to the compliance filing.
points.quote: SPP's Board of Directors meeting is scheduled for November 17, 2026—one day outside the 90-day window.

points.point: It cites the 12-month Order No. 1920 extension FERC gave SPP in April 2025 as precedent for good cause.
points.quote: the Commission granted SPP a 12-month extension of time to submit filings in compliance with the Commission's Order No. 1920

points.point: State regulators care about transparency and cost-shift avoidance because they set retail rates that include transmission costs.
points.quote: Issues related to transparency and the avoidance of cost shifting are particularly important to the Missouri PSC and other state regulators who bear the responsibility of setting retail rates

points.point: The abeyance gives the CARE Team time to finish cost mitigation recommendations for the Board.
points.quote: The requested abeyance will allow the CARE Team time to complete this important work and present its recommendations to the Board.

throughLine.text: Supports the E-9 SPP abeyance motion and ties the extra five days to state-regulator review of the cost-shift protections the order directs SPP to address.

figures.label: Abeyance requested for SPP show cause proceeding
figures.quote: The Joint Movants asked to hold the proceedings in abeyance for 95 days, up to and including November 20, 2026.
